methodological_rigor.justification: Competent experimental design with appropriate controls, biological replication across two LUSC cell lines (NCI-H226, NCI-H520), and validated cell lines (STR analysis). Standard statistical tests (ANOVA, t-tests, Pearson correlation) applied correctly. However, gaps include: no in vivo validation, single mechanistic pathway focus, lack of pre-registration, and missing effect sizes or confidence intervals in most figures. Statistical approach adequate but without multiplicity correction or power calculations.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical mechanistic study using cell lines and bioinformatics analysis only; classified as LoE 5 per Oxford CEBM. Translational path is speculative and complicated by an unresolved paradox: low HP expression correlates with poor prognosis in LUSC patient data, yet HP overexpression promotes M2 macrophage ferroptosis in vitro. Authors acknowledge this contradiction and propose 'compensatory recruitment,' but mechanism remains unvalidated in vivo. Clinical applicability is limited without patient-level or in vivo model validation.

reporting_quality.justification: Adequate reporting of Methods (lentiviral vectors, cell culture, molecular techniques), Results (clear flow cytometry panels, TEM images, statistical summaries), and Discussion. However, no data availability statement or mention of code/supplementary material sharing. CIBERSORT parameters are redacted ('REDACTED accessed in September 2025'). No explicit adherence to ARRIVE reporting checklist. Reproducibility is limited by reliance on proprietary commercial cell lines and incomplete methodological transparency.

novelty_literature.justification: Systematic bioinformatics approach (network analysis, pathway enrichment, Kaplan-Meier survival) identifies HP as a hub gene in LUSC with prognostic relevance—a meaningful contribution. Mechanistic finding extends prior knowledge about iron recycling in M2 macrophages by linking HP to CD163/HO-1-mediated ferroptosis. However, ferroptosis in cancer and M2 macrophage biology are well-established; this represents an incremental application to LUSC rather than a novel mechanism. Not duplicative but a one-directional extension of existing knowledge.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear structure (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion), logical narrative flow, and readable scientific English. Figures are informative (Kaplan-Meier curves, flow cytometry overlays, TEM micrographs) and appropriately cited. Discussion thoughtfully addresses the central in vitro/in vivo paradox and proposes 'compensatory recruitment' hypothesis. Minor issues: some figures are dense (multiple panels, small fonts), Results section has high information density, and limitation discussion leans speculative rather than concrete.

key_strengths: Systematic multi-algorithm bioinformatics approach (MCC, MNC, degree, EPC, closeness, radiality) identifies HP as a hub gene with prognostic association in LUSC (Kaplan-Meier, p=0.049)

Rigorous in vitro mechanistic validation using multiple ferroptosis markers (LDH release, 7-AAD membrane permeability, FerroOrange Fe2+, BODIPY lipid peroxides, TEM ultrastructure) across two cell lines with biological replication
Clear acknowledgment of study limitations including lack of in vivo validation, species-specific differences in HP-Hb-CD163 binding, and oversimplification of the tumor microenvironment in vitro

Well-organized presentation with informative figures and thoughtful Discussion addressing the paradox between patient data (low HP predicts poor prognosis) and in vitro findings (HP promotes M2 ferroptosis)
key_concerns: Complete absence of in vivo validation in LUSC xenografts, syngeneic models, or patient-derived specimens severely limits translational confidence and clinical applicability

Unresolved central paradox: low HP correlates with worse prognosis in LUSC patients, yet HP overexpression promotes M2 ferroptosis in vitro; proposed 'compensatory recruitment' mechanism is speculative without mechanistic support
Preclinical study (LoE 5) with no clear path to drug targeting; HP therapeutic druggability not addressed and compensatory immunological responses in vivo remain unexplored
Limited novelty—applies established ferroptosis and macrophage iron-recycling biology (CD163/HO-1/HMOX1 axis) to one acute-phase protein without revelation of new mechanistic insights
No data or code availability; reproducibility contingent on proprietary cell lines (no access) and CIBERSORT parameters redacted; missing effect sizes and confidence intervals in key comparisons
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competently executed preclinical mechanistic study appropriate for a specialized oncology journal (Tier 3, 4-9.9 JIF range: Cancers, Frontiers in Oncology, BMC Cancer). The bioinformatics approach is systematic and the in vitro experiments are rigorous, but the work lacks in vivo validation, presents an unresolved in vitro/in vivo paradox regarding HP's clinical role, and offers incremental rather than paradigm-shifting novelty. Minor revisions addressing data availability, effect sizes, and expanded discussion of the paradox would support publication at Tier 3.
